outputText: We need answer user: "Explain why local inference benchmarks should report prompt prefill throughput, decode throughput, and time to first token." Need provide explanation. Need final answer. Need likely discuss LLM inference phases: prefill/prompt processing vs decode token generation. Local benchmarks need these metrics because they capture different bottlenecks: prefill throughput (tokens/s for prompt) measures how fast model can process input context, KV cache build, attention over prompt, batched prompt, memory bandwidth/compute, affects latency for long contexts and RAG. Decode throughput (tokens/s generated) measures autoregressive generation speed, often memory-bandwidth bound, affects sustained output speed. TTFT (time to first token) measures user-perceived latency from request to first generated token, includes prompt prefill, scheduling, loading, overhead; important for interactive use. Reporting all three avoids misleading single throughput number: a model may have high decode but slow prefill, or low TTFT but poor sustained throughput; prompt length and output length matter. Also local inference specifics: CPU/GPU, quantization, batch size, context length, hardware constraints, KV cache memory, offloading. Need maybe mention prompt prefill throughput vs decode throughput can differ orders of magnitude; prefill is compute-bound
